title: Couple found dead at Nuevo Laredo motel; carbon monoxide poisoning investigated
excerpt: A man and a woman were found dead inside a room at the Motel Emirato in Nuevo Laredo. Authorities are investigating whether carbon monoxide poisoning caused their deaths.
content:
A man and a woman were found dead inside a room at the Motel Emirato in Nuevo Laredo on Monday, and authorities are investigating whether carbon monoxide poisoning caused their deaths.

Emergency responders were called to the motel after the two people were found in the room. When responders arrived, both victims had no vital signs.

A pickup truck was left running in the motel's garage, and investigators believe it may have caused the poisoning.

Authorities are treating carbon monoxide poisoning as one of the main hypotheses, but the cause of death will be determined through the investigation and forensic studies. The bodies were taken for forensic examinations.

No names or ages for the victims have been released. Authorities are working to determine what conditions allowed the gas to accumulate in the room.

Update — November 25, 2026

Relatives have identified the two people found dead as Jesús Antonio and Emma Paola, who were cousins, according to El Horizonte and other Mexican outlets. Emma Paola’s father and an uncle of both recognized the bodies. Jesús Antonio worked as an escort for oversize cargo transport in Laredo, Texas, and Emma Paola worked as a private nurse, according to the reports. Relatives told authorities the pickup truck had been having mechanical trouble for days and may have been left running because they feared it would not start again.

The cause of death has still not been officially confirmed. The Tamaulipas Attorney General’s Office is investigating, and the bodies were taken for forensic examination; the necropsy will determine the exact cause of death, according to the reports.

Update sources: El Horizonte, Nov. 23, 2026; Central Noticias Tamaulipas, Nov. 25, 2026; UXAJU, Nov. 23, 2026.
